claims.text: HfNbTiVAl10 has a hierarchical heterostructure with multilevel chemical fluctuations.
A reduced-order physics-informed ML model can combine localized imaging-derived microstructural descriptors with simplified physics-based features.
Ab initio-derived descriptors or inputs can be combined with experimental data in ML models.
Minimal ab initio inputs can calibrate elastic and fracture-mechanics parameters for the proposed reduced-order model.
High-resolution imaging can quantify grain boundaries, phase distributions, and chemical-fluctuation zones that are representative of the tested specimens.
The selected localized microstructural features act as descriptors of elastic anisotropy and crack initiation and propagation.
Encoding structural heterogeneity and simplified elastic-anisotropy and crack-propagation relationships will reduce computational intensity.
Encoding structural heterogeneity and simplified physics will improve predictions of Young's modulus and yield strength.
Encoding structural heterogeneity and simplified crack-propagation physics will improve predictions of toughness.
The framework will predict Young's modulus and yield strength within 10% of standardized test results.
The framework will predict toughness within 15% of standardized fracture-test results.
The framework will reduce computational time by up to one order of magnitude.
The framework will improve predictive accuracy by 20–30% relative to conventional methods.
Ab initio and molecular-dynamics approaches are too time-consuming for efficient high-throughput alloy-structure prediction, while CALPHAD can require significant computing resources.
Conventional ML approaches can require large datasets, are sensitive to training-set composition, and cannot reliably extrapolate outside the covered data domain.
The proposed model may become unreliable when testing conditions lie outside its calibrated domain, including extreme temperatures and very high strain rates.
The proposed model may become unreliable for highly irregular hierarchical heterostructures or emergent phenomena absent from its descriptors.
Analogous hybrid models in the literature suggest a 20–30% accuracy improvement and an order-of-magnitude reduction in computational demand.
A blinded prospective benchmark will compare predictions on controlled, microstructurally varied HfNbTiVAl10 specimens with independently collected tensile and fracture-test measurements.
The hypothesis is falsified if any Young's-modulus or yield-strength prediction differs by more than 10%, or any toughness prediction differs by more than 15%, from measurement.
